oneTimers: Paper losses on investments: 'Other (gains) and losses' was a $597M loss, mostly from marking down the value of equity stakes Walmart holds — a year ago the same line was a $794M gain. The stores themselves had a solid quarter.
otherDetail: A $597M loss on equity and other investments, plus $544M of net interest expense. Noncontrolling interests took a $152M share of the profit, which is removed to reach profit attributable to Walmart.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The main store business — comparable sales rose 4.5%, led by grocery and health & wellness.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores outside the U.S. — China grew while Mexico and Central America sales slipped in dollar terms.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Membership fees and other income — nearly pure profit.

takeaways.text: The retail business itself improved — U.S. comparable sales rose 4.5% and the gross profit rate widened — even as headline profit fell on paper investment losses.
takeaways.title: Operating income rose 4.3%

takeaways.text: Online sales grew 22% globally, and the global advertising business grew 50% including VIZIO — higher-margin income growing far faster than store sales.
takeaways.title: eCommerce is the growth engine

takeaways.text: Excluding the paper investment losses and other items, adjusted EPS was $0.61 versus GAAP EPS of $0.56.
takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS tells the cleaner story

verdict: Walmart's revenue grew 2.5% to $165.6B and operating income rose 4% — but a $597M paper loss on its investment stakes cut headline profit 12% to $4.5B.
